intro: Request-level test cases for the Stage-5 supplier-PO API: supplier master + CRUD, PO generation from a BOM, the cross-check state machine, send/acknowledge, the unauthenticated tracking + webhook routes, and the production board. Every row is a literal HTTP request with the exact status code and response fields to check.
notes: **MD and DM bypass every `require_roles` gate** (`SUPERUSER_ROLES` in `app/modules/users/deps.py`). So a DM passes the MD-only supplier delete/reactivate gate. Any case that says "MD-only" is MD-only *in intent*; verify what the build actually does.

**Approver routing is enforced in the service, not the router.** `_APPROVERS` admits Cutting Manager / MD / DM / HR, then `PoService._assert_router_role` narrows: leather POs → {Cutting Manager, MD}, accessory/service POs → {MD, DM, HR}. MD short-circuits everything; **DM does not** — a DM approving a leather PO is expected to get 403 `wrong_approver` despite bypassing the router gate.

**Two error shapes.** Router/`_load` failures are plain `{"detail": "..."}` strings (404s, role 403s, 413, the tracking 400). Service failures are dicts: `{"error": "...", "message"?: "...", ...}`. Assert both shapes.

**The tracking (`/t/o/…`, `/t/c/…`) and webhook (`/webhooks/…`) routes have no auth dependency at all** — by design, since a supplier's mail client, Twilio and SES call them. Provider signature verification is still marked TODO in the router, so today anyone who can reach those URLs can forge a delivery/bounce event or a supplier acknowledgement. J-L1 covers this.
A malformed (non-UUID) path parameter returns a generic **422** from FastAPI's own path parsing, before any handler runs — distinct from the 404 raised for a well-formed but nonexistent id.
`PoBulkPatch.base_revision` is `ge=1`; always take the live `revision` from a fresh `GET /pos/{id}` rather than sending 0.
PO numbers are minted on the **first** send only, from a financial-year series; `issue_date` and `tracking_token` are set at the same moment.

cases.title: Preview a supplier workbook
steps: multipart body: file = <the supplier contact + provision workbook>
cases.expected: 200 with the preview block: contact_rows, provision_rows, suppliers, suppliers_with_phone, suppliers_with_email, history_rows, warnings[], sample_history[] (capped at 25). Nothing is persisted — a follow-up GET /suppliers is unchanged.

cases.title: Commit the same workbook
cases.expected: 200 with the same preview block plus committed, history_rows and deactivated. Suppliers are upserted, supply history is rebuilt wholesale and an AuditLog row with action SUPPLIER_IMPORT is written.

cases.title: Wrong role imports
cases.expected: {"detail":"Role 'cutting_manager' is not permitted for this action"} — import is DM/MD only.

cases.title: No file part
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/suppliers/import/preview with an empty body (no multipart file field)
cases.expected: 422 — FastAPI's File(...) is required, so the request never reaches the service.

cases.title: Upload over the size cap
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/suppliers/import/preview — file = <a workbook larger than MAX_UPLOAD_MB (25 MB default)>
cases.expected: 413 {"detail":"File exceeds the 25 MB limit."} — raised by _read_capped while streaming, before the parser runs.

cases.title: Empty or unparseable file
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/suppliers/import/preview — file = <0 bytes, or a .txt renamed .xlsx>
cases.expected: Expect a clean 4xx or a preview with warnings — NOT a 500. The router has no content-type check, so whatever the parser does is the whole defence; record the actual behaviour.

cases.title: Re-import never blanks a known contact
steps: PATCH a supplier to add an email/phone by hand
POST /api/v1/procurement/suppliers/import/commit with a workbook where that supplier has NO email/phone
cases.expected: The hand-entered email/phone survives — commit uses `existing.phone or s.phone`, so an import can fill a blank but never overwrite a known value with nothing.

cases.title: Absent suppliers are soft-deactivated, never deleted
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/suppliers/import/commit with a workbook that omits a previously imported supplier
cases.expected: The response's `deactivated` count includes that supplier and it still exists with is_active:false. No row is ever hard-deleted.

cases.title: Supply history is rebuilt wholesale
steps: Commit workbook v1, note a supplier's history rows via GET /suppliers/{id}
Commit workbook v2 in which that supplier has fewer article rows
cases.expected: History is cleared and re-inserted from the new file, so rows only present in v1 are gone — history is a mirror of the latest import, not an accumulation.

cases.title: List suppliers
cases.expected: 200 {"suppliers":[{id,name,phone,email,service,supplier_type,is_active,…}], "count": N}.

cases.title: Filter the list
cases.expected: 200; every row matches the filters. `count` is the length of THIS page, not the total matching set — don't paginate off it.

cases.title: Read one supplier
cases.expected: 200 — the supplier block enriched with its supply `history` and `open_pos`.

cases.title: Office Viewer can read
cases.expected: 200 — VIEWER is inside the _VIEW read gate, unlike every mutating route in this module.

cases.title: Unknown supplier id
cases.expected: 404 {"detail":"Supplier not found."}

cases.title: Malformed supplier id
cases.expected: 422 from FastAPI's path parsing — the handler never runs, so the shape differs from B-N1's 404.

cases.title: Role outside the read gate
cases.expected: 403 role-not-permitted — Cutting Manager can approve leather POs but cannot browse the supplier master.

cases.title: limit=0 and a far offset
cases.expected: 200 with an empty list and count:0 in both cases — limit/offset carry no bounds or validation at all.

cases.title: Unbounded limit
cases.expected: 200, accepted — there is no server-side ceiling on `limit`. Flag as a possible DoS/perf gap on a large master.

cases.title: Deactivated suppliers appear unless filtered out
cases.expected: The deactivated supplier is still listed — `active` defaults to None, which applies no filter. A picker UI must pass active=true explicitly or it will offer dead vendors.

cases.title: Create with just a name
cases.expected: 201 with the supplier block. Defaults applied: currency INR, payment_terms_days 60, lead_time_days 10, is_active true, email_status "unknown" (no email given).

cases.title: Create with contact details
cases.expected: 201; email_status "valid" because an email was supplied, whatsapp_phone falls back to `phone`, and state_code is derived from the GSTIN's first two digits (33).

cases.title: Add an email to a contactless vendor
cases.expected: 200; email_status flips to "valid", which is what unblocks the §5 send path for a vendor previously marked invalid by a bounce.

cases.title: Fix a GSTIN
cases.expected: 200; state_code is re-derived (27), which flips later PO totals between CGST+SGST and IGST.

cases.title: Deactivate then reactivate
cases.expected: {"id":…,"is_active":false} then {"id":…,"is_active":true}. DELETE is a soft deactivate — the row, its history and its POs all survive.

cases.title: Duplicate supplier name
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/suppliers — Body: {"name":"<the exact name of an existing supplier>"}
cases.expected: 409 {"error":"duplicate_name","name":"…"}

cases.title: Empty name
cases.expected: Both 422, but from different layers: "" fails Pydantic's min_length=1 (generic shape); "   " passes Pydantic and is caught by the service as {"error":"name_required"}.

cases.title: Wrong role creates
cases.expected: 403 role-not-permitted.

cases.title: Patch an unknown supplier
cases.expected: 404 {"detail":"Supplier not found."}

cases.title: Empty patch body
cases.expected: 200 and nothing changes — the router drops None fields with exclude_none before the service sees them.

cases.title: Nonsense numeric terms
cases.expected: 201, accepted — neither field has a ge/le bound in SupplierCreate. Note that 0 is falsy, so lead_time_days:0 is replaced by the default 10 while -30 is stored as-is. Flag both as validation gaps.

cases.title: A DM can delete despite the MD-only gate
steps: DELETE /api/v1/procurement/suppliers/{supplier_id} as a DIRECT MANAGER (the route is gated require_roles(MANAGING_DIRECTOR))
cases.expected: 200, not 403 — DIRECT_MANAGER is in SUPERUSER_ROLES and bypasses every require_roles gate. The MD-only intent of this route is not enforced today; confirm and report.

cases.title: PATCH can never clear a field
cases.expected: 200, but the email is unchanged — nulls are stripped by exclude_none AND skipped again in the service loop. There is no way to remove a wrong email through this API; confirm and flag.

cases.title: Duplicate detection is exact-name only
cases.expected: Verify whether the second call 409s or creates a second row. The duplicate guard keys on the stored name; if it is case/whitespace sensitive, near-duplicate vendors can be created and will then compete in PO matching.

cases.title: Generate from a checked BOM with shortfalls
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/boms/{bom_id}/generate-pos (BOM approved/locked, inventory check run, at least one short line)
cases.expected: 200 {"bom_id":…,"purchase_orders":[…]} — one draft PO per matched supplier, carrying only the shortfall lines.

cases.title: Re-generate is idempotent
cases.expected: 200 {"already_generated":true,"purchase_orders":[…]} — the existing POs are returned, no duplicates are created.

cases.title: Nothing is short
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/boms/{bom_id}/generate-pos on a BOM whose every checked line came back sufficient
cases.expected: 200 with purchase_orders: [] — a clean "nothing to buy" answer, not an error.

cases.title: No inventory check yet
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/boms/{bom_id}/generate-pos on a BOM that has never been inventory-checked
cases.expected: 409 {"error":"no_inventory_check","message":"Run the inventory check before generating supplier POs."} — the check is a hard precondition.

cases.title: Unknown BOM
cases.expected: 404 {"detail":"BOM not found."}

cases.title: Wrong role generates
cases.expected: 403 — a viewer can read POs but cannot raise them.

cases.title: Generate after cancelling every PO
steps: Cancel every PO previously generated for the BOM (POST /pos/{po_id}/cancel)
cases.expected: 200 with FRESH purchase orders, not already_generated — cancelled POs are excluded from the "already generated" test, which is the documented re-issue path for a sent PO.

cases.title: Unmatched lines still produce a PO
steps: Generate for a BOM containing a material no supplier history matches
cases.expected: The line lands on a PO with needs_supplier:true and no supplier_id. It is visible in the needs-supplier worklist and will be refused at submit (G-N1) until a supplier is assigned via PATCH.

cases.title: Only shortfall lines are bought
steps: Compare the inventory check's lines (GET /boms/{bom_id}/inventory-check) with the generated POs' lines
cases.expected: Only lines whose status is not `sufficient` AND whose shortfall_qty > 0 appear on a PO; the PO quantity is the shortfall, not the full BOM requirement.

cases.title: List POs
cases.expected: 200 with the PO list — each row carrying status, supplier, needs_supplier, revision and totals.

cases.title: Filter the list
cases.expected: 200 each; every row matches the filter. needs_supplier=true is the assignment worklist.

cases.title: Read one PO
cases.expected: 200 — full PO view: items[], revision, subtotal, cgst/sgst/igst, gst_mode, round_off, total, status, and the tracking/acknowledgement fields once sent.

cases.title: Unknown PO id
cases.expected: 404 {"detail":"Purchase order not found."}

cases.title: Wrong role reads
cases.expected: 403 — note the asymmetry: a Cutting Manager may be the required APPROVER of a leather PO (G-P2) yet cannot list POs through this endpoint. Worth flagging as a workflow gap.

cases.title: Nonsense status filter
cases.expected: 200 with an empty list — `status` is a free string with no enum validation, so a typo yields "no results" rather than a 422. Flag it.

cases.title: The approver cannot browse what they must approve
steps: As Cutting Manager: POST /api/v1/procurement/pos/{po_id}/approve on a leather PO → 200
cases.expected: Confirms E-N2: the approval notification link is the only way a Cutting Manager can reach a PO, because the read gate excludes them. File as a finding.

cases.title: Edit qty and unit price
cases.expected: 200 {"revision": base_revision+1, "recomputed": {…}} — line amounts, subtotal, tax and total all recomputed in the same response.

cases.title: Add a line
cases.expected: 200; the new line appears in recomputed.items with the next line number and is included in the totals.

cases.title: Remove a line
cases.expected: 200; the line is gone from recomputed.items and the totals drop accordingly.

cases.title: Assign the missing supplier
cases.expected: 200; needs_supplier flips to false, match_method becomes "manual", and no_contact_channel reflects whether that supplier has an email or phone.

cases.title: Stale revision
steps: Both sessions GET the PO and note revision N
Session A: PATCH with base_revision N → succeeds
Session B: PATCH with base_revision N, sent after A
cases.expected: A: 200. B: 409 {"error":"stale_revision","current_revision":N+1} — enforced twice: a pre-check and an atomic claim_po_revision at commit, so a true race cannot slip through.

cases.title: Edit a sent PO
steps: PATCH /api/v1/procurement/pos/{po_id}/items on a PO whose status is sent / responded / confirmed / escalated
cases.expected: 409 {"error":"po_locked","message":"A sent PO is frozen — cancel + re-issue."}

cases.title: Unknown line id
steps: PATCH …/items — Body: {"base_revision":1,"item_edits":[{"po_item_id":"<a uuid not on this PO>","field":"qty","value":5}]}
cases.expected: 422 {"error":"unknown_po_item","po_item_id":"…"}

cases.title: Unsupported field
cases.expected: 422 {"error":"unsupported_field","field":"amount"} — only description, color, uom, qty and unit_price are editable; `amount` is derived.

cases.title: Non-numeric quantity
cases.expected: 422 {"error":"invalid_value","field":"qty"} — the service's own Decimal coercion, not Pydantic (PoItemEdit.value is typed `object`).

cases.title: Assign an unknown or inactive supplier
cases.expected: 422 {"error":"unknown_supplier"} — a deactivated supplier is refused exactly like a nonexistent one, so you cannot route a PO to a dead vendor.

cases.title: base_revision 0
cases.expected: 422 — PoBulkPatch enforces ge=1. Always copy the live revision from a fresh GET.

cases.title: A patch that changes nothing
steps: PATCH …/items — Body: {"base_revision": 1}   (no edits, no adds, no removes)
cases.expected: 200 and the revision still increments — an empty save burns a revision and will stale-out anyone else holding the old number. Confirm and note.

cases.title: Remove a line that isn't on the PO
steps: PATCH …/items — Body: {"base_revision":1,"remove_item_ids":["<a uuid not on this PO>"]}
cases.expected: 200, silently ignored — unlike item_edits (F-N3), removals of unknown ids raise nothing. Asymmetric; flag it.

cases.title: Negative quantity or price
cases.expected: 200, accepted — the service only coerces to Decimal, it never checks the sign, so a negative line amount flows into the PO total and the PDF. Flag as a money-path validation gap.

cases.title: Changing supplier resets an approval
steps: Take a PO to status approved
cases.expected: 200; status is back to "draft" and approved_by/approved_at are cleared — a new supplier may route to a different approver class, so the old approval cannot stand.

cases.title: GST mode follows the supplier's state
steps: Assign a supplier whose GSTIN state matches PO_BUYER_STATE_CODE, PATCH any line, read recomputed
Assign a supplier in a different state, PATCH again, read recomputed
cases.expected: Intra-state: cgst and sgst populated, igst zero. Inter-state: igst populated, cgst/sgst zero. gst_mode names which was applied and round_off balances the total.

cases.title: Edits are audited before and after
steps: Inspect the AuditLog rows (DB or an audit endpoint) for action PO_EDIT
cases.expected: One PO_EDIT row per patch carrying both the before and after snapshots — the money trail for a changed PO.

sections.title: Cross-check state machine
sections.gate: DM / MD (submit, cancel) · Cutting Manager / MD / DM / HR (approve, reject — narrowed by the service)

cases.title: Submit a draft for cross-check
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/pos/{po_id}/submit (status draft, supplier assigned, at least one line)
cases.expected: 200 {"po_id":…,"status":"pending_approval","notifications_created":N} — N in-app notifications, one per user in the routed approver class.

cases.title: Cutting Manager approves a leather PO
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/pos/{po_id}/approve on a PO whose supplier_type is leather
cases.expected: 200 {"po_id":…,"status":"approved"} — leather routes to {Cutting Manager, MD}.

cases.title: HR approves an accessory PO
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/pos/{po_id}/approve on a PO whose supplier_type is accessory or service
cases.expected: 200 approved — accessory/service routes to {MD, DM, HR}.

cases.title: Reject with a reason
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/pos/{po_id}/reject — Body: {"reason":"Rate is above the last purchase price"}
cases.expected: 200 {"po_id":…,"status":"rejected","rejection_reason":"Rate is above the last purchase price"} — the reason is stored trimmed.

cases.title: Cancel a draft
cases.expected: 200 {"po_id":…,"status":"cancelled"}; the BOM can then be re-generated (D-B1).

cases.title: Submit without a supplier
cases.expected: 409 {"error":"needs_supplier","message":"Assign a supplier before submitting."}

cases.title: Submit an empty PO
cases.expected: 409 {"error":"empty_po"}

cases.title: Submit from the wrong state
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/pos/{po_id}/submit on a PO already approved / sent / cancelled
cases.expected: 409 {"error":"not_submittable","current_status":"…"} — only draft and rejected are submittable.

cases.title: Approve something not awaiting approval
cases.expected: 409 {"error":"not_pending_approval","current_status":"draft"} — note this is stricter than the BOM's approve, which never re-checks status.

cases.title: Wrong approver class
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/pos/{po_id}/approve on a LEATHER PO as HR
cases.expected: 403 {"error":"wrong_approver","message":"This PO routes to ['cutting_manager', 'managing_director']."} — HR passes the router gate and is then refused by the service's routing check.

cases.title: Reject with no real reason
cases.expected: "" → 422 from Pydantic (min_length=1). "   " → 422 {"error":"reason_required"} from the service. Two shapes, same intent.

cases.title: Cancel a sent PO
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/pos/{po_id}/cancel on a PO already sent
cases.expected: 409 {"error":"po_locked","message":"A sent PO cannot be cancelled in place."} — a supplier already has this document; it must be superseded, not silently voided.

cases.title: MD approves anything
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/pos/{po_id}/approve on a leather PO as MD
and again on an accessory PO
cases.expected: 200 both times — _assert_router_role returns immediately for MANAGING_DIRECTOR, before any routing is computed.

cases.title: Double-click approve
cases.expected: First 200, second 409 not_pending_approval — the repeat fails safely rather than re-stamping approved_at.

cases.title: Very long rejection reason
cases.expected: 200; the GET returns the full text untruncated.

cases.title: Reject → fix → resubmit is a closed loop
cases.expected: The resubmit succeeds — `rejected` is explicitly submittable, so one rejection does not strand the PO. Confirm the notifications fire again for the approver class.

cases.title: A DM cannot approve a leather PO
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/pos/{po_id}/approve on a LEATHER PO as a DIRECT MANAGER
cases.expected: 403 wrong_approver — DM bypasses the router's role gate (SUPERUSER_ROLES) but _assert_router_role only short-circuits for MD, and DM is not in _LEATHER_APPROVERS. This is the one MD-only rule in the module the DM bypass does NOT defeat; confirm it holds.

cases.title: Only the routed class is notified
steps: Submit a leather PO, note notifications_created
cases.expected: The Cutting Manager (and MD) receive a PO_AWAITING_APPROVAL notification; HR does not. For an accessory PO the reverse holds. Recipients are de-duplicated and the notification's scheduled_for is the escalation deadline.

cases.title: Send an approved PO
cases.expected: 200; the PO now has a po_number from the financial-year series, issue_date = today, a tracking_token, a stored PDF, and status "sent". The escalation clock starts here.

cases.title: Record a manual acknowledgement
cases.expected: 200 with the PO view; acknowledged_at is stamped and the escalation ladder stops immediately.

cases.title: Send before approval
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/pos/{po_id}/send on a draft or pending_approval PO
cases.expected: 409 {"error":"not_approved","current_status":"…"}

cases.title: Wrong role sends
cases.expected: 403 role-not-permitted.

cases.title: Send twice
cases.expected: 409 not_approved with current_status "sent" — re-sending is not an idempotent replay here (unlike the BOM export); to contact the supplier again you go through the escalation ladder.

cases.title: Acknowledge twice
cases.expected: Both 200, but the second is a no-op returning the existing view — _acknowledge returns early once acknowledged_at is set, so the first acknowledgement wins and the later notes are silently dropped. Confirm and note.

cases.title: The PO number is minted once
steps: Trigger any later state change (acknowledge, escalate) and GET the PO again
cases.expected: po_number and issue_date never change after the first send — the number is the supplier-facing identity of the document.

cases.title: Any channel stops the ladder
steps: Acknowledge it through ANY route: this endpoint, the WhatsApp webhook, or the voice webhook (J-P2 / J-P3)
cases.expected: acknowledged_at is set once and the escalation ladder (email → WhatsApp → call) stops, regardless of which channel got there first.

cases.title: The open pixel records an open
cases.expected: 200 with content-type image/gif (the 1×1 pixel) and an `open` tracking event recorded against the PO. Sending a token belonging to a sent PO should also move the response status toward opened.

cases.title: A signed click redirects
steps: (disable redirect-following in the client so you can see the 302 itself)
cases.expected: 302 with a Location header pointing at the unwrapped target URL, and a `click` event recorded.

cases.title: Click with a bad signature
steps: and again with the s parameter omitted entirely
cases.expected: 400 {"detail":"Invalid tracking link."} both times — the redirect target is HMAC-verified against SECRET_KEY, so this endpoint cannot be used as an open redirect.

cases.title: Pixel with an unknown token
cases.expected: Still 200 with the pixel — an unknown token records nothing but must not 404, or a scanner could enumerate valid tokens by status code. Confirm no information leaks through timing or body either.

cases.title: The same pixel loaded many times
steps: GET the same /t/o/{token}.gif five times (as a mail client re-rendering would)
cases.expected: 200 each time; multiple open events are logged. Decide whether the engagement view should de-duplicate — a Gmail image proxy alone can inflate this.

cases.title: These routes are exempt from auth by design
steps: Call both /t/o/… and /t/c/… with no Authorization header, and again with a garbage bearer token
cases.expected: No 401 in any of the four calls — the opaque per-send token IS the credential. Verify the token is unguessable (po_tracking.new_token) and that neither response exposes PO contents, supplier data or ids.

cases.title: SES delivery and bounce events
cases.expected: {"ok":true} both times; a delivery and a bounce event are logged. The bounce should mark the supplier's email_status invalid, which blocks further email sends until a new address is patched in (C-P3).

cases.title: WhatsApp reply acknowledges the PO
cases.expected: {"ok":true}; the PO is acknowledged with channel whatsapp and the reply text stored in notes.

cases.title: Voice press-1 acknowledges, press-2 does not
cases.expected: Both return {"ok":true}, but only the Digits "1" call sets acknowledged_at — the handler compares the digit explicitly.

cases.title: Payload with no tracking token
cases.expected: {"ok":true} and nothing recorded — a missing token is silently ignored, never an error, because a provider retrying on a 4xx would be worse.

cases.title: Body that isn't a JSON object
steps: POST /api/v1/procurement/webhooks/ses with Body: "just a string"  (or malformed JSON)
cases.expected: 422 — the handler is typed `payload: dict`, so a non-object body is refused by FastAPI before any processing.

cases.title: Unknown token in a webhook
cases.expected: {"ok":true} — acknowledge_by_token returns False for an unknown token and the handler ignores the result. No 404, nothing recorded.

cases.title: SES payload with the token nested under mail
cases.expected: {"ok":true} and the event is recorded — the handler falls back to payload["mail"]["tracking_token"] and accepts eventType, notificationType or type as the event name.

cases.title: Webhook signatures are not verified
steps: From any client, POST /api/v1/procurement/webhooks/twilio/whatsapp with a valid tracking_token you obtained from a PO
cases.expected: The PO is acknowledged even though the request came from nobody in particular — the router's own docstring marks provider signature verification TODO. Anyone able to reach the URL with a token can forge an acknowledgement or a bounce. Confirm and file as a security finding with the token's exposure surface (it travels in every tracked email link).

sections.title: Production board
sections.gate: DM / MD / Viewer (read) · MD / DM / Cutting Manager (transition)

cases.title: Read the board
cases.expected: 200 with one row per tracked style/order — client, order, style and the ladder status (awaiting_bom → bom_approved → inventory_checked → po_raised → po_confirmed → material_ready → released_to_production → in_production → completed). The filtered call returns a subset.

cases.title: The human go/no-go transition
cases.expected: 200 {"id":…,"status":"released_to_production"} — this is the deliberate manual gate; the earlier rungs advance automatically from BOM approval, the inventory check and PO confirmation.

cases.title: Unknown status value
cases.expected: 422 {"error":"unknown_status","status":"shipped"} — the target must be one of the ProductionTrackingStatus values.

cases.title: Unknown tracker id
cases.expected: 404 {"detail":"Tracker not found."}

cases.title: Wrong role transitions
cases.expected: 403 — the router gate admits MD/DM/Cutting only, and the service repeats the check with the message "Only DM/MD/Cutting may transition the board."

cases.title: Empty status string
cases.expected: 422 from Pydantic (min_length=1), before the unknown_status check runs.

cases.title: Transition backwards down the ladder
cases.expected: 200 — manual transitions call _advance with force=True, so the ladder is not monotonic and a finished order can be dragged back to an early rung. Intentional for corrections, but confirm it is what the business wants and that the move is audited.

cases.title: The board mirrors the upstream stages
steps: Approve its BOM, then run the inventory check, then generate and confirm a PO
cases.expected: The row advances on its own through bom_approved → inventory_checked → po_raised → po_confirmed without any manual transition. Only released_to_production requires a human.
